questions.q: The sigmoid derivative $f'(z) = f(z)\,(1 - f(z))$ is at most $0.25$. In the Backprop Race, what is the **best case** fraction of the error that survives 3 sigmoid layers?
questions.explain: The chain rule multiplies one derivative per layer: $0.25 \times 0.25 \times 0.25 = 0.015625$. Even at the ideal $z = 0$ sigmoid loses ~98% of the gradient; adding the factors (75%) is the common mistake.

questions.q: What is the tanh derivative $f'(z) = 1 - \tanh^2(z)$ at $z = 1$?
questions.explain: $\tanh(1) \approx 0.762$, so $1 - 0.762^2 \approx 0.42$. $1$ is the peak at $z = 0$, $0.76$ is $\tanh(1)$ itself, and $0.07$ is the derivative at $z = 2$: it drops quickly as $|z|$ grows.

questions.q: At the preset 'Deep Negative' ($z = -3$), what do ReLU and Leaky ReLU ($\alpha = 0.1$) output, and what are their derivatives?
questions.explain: ReLU $= \max(0, z)$ blocks negative inputs completely. Leaky ReLU $= \max(0.1z, z) = -0.3$ and keeps a small slope $0.1$, so a gradient still leaks through and the unit can recover.

questions.q: When is a ReLU unit called a **dead ReLU**?
options: When it is inactive (input ≤ 0) for every input in the data, so it never receives a gradient again
Whenever its input is negative for a single example
When its output is larger than 1
questions.explain: A negative input only blocks the gradient *for that input*. The unit is 'dead' when it sits in the flat zero region for **all** inputs, so its weights stop updating permanently.
